items.title: Clarence Gabriel Interview
items.q: He laid on Albert Fernandes playing piano with him.

ctx.x: That was near Ramport Street then?

The Budweiser, no. The front was near Ramport. Close to the Ramport. Close to the Ramport. That was some rough days. The Budweiser went there. The Budweiser went there in 1930. We would come off to Dixie. The Budweiser was looking for us and he came. That's when we went to the Laveena. Mike stayed there. Mike stayed there a long time. He laid on Albert Fernandes playing piano with him. He'd swap up the trumpet to piano. See, Albert played piano and he played piano. He'd swap up and let the rest of the lip up.…

I was going to ask some more about some of the pieces that you played with Louis Demain. Did he write many numbers? I know when he made the records he had the number he called Franklin Street Blues and Red Onion Drag. I wonder, did you ever play those in the dance band that you worked with him?
